q: A bank needs near-zero data loss and failover in seconds for a payment platform, while accepting higher cost. Which design is MOST appropriate?
opts: A single zone with a larger instance type and frequent snapshots
Weekly full backups copied to cold storage in another region
Active-active deployment across availability zones with synchronous replication
A pilot light environment with asynchronous replication to a second region
why: Only active-active with synchronous replication supports near-zero RPO and fast failover. Backups and pilot light have longer recovery, and a single zone is a single failure domain.

q: A planner proposes selecting a disaster recovery technology before the business impact analysis is complete. What is the BEST response?
opts: Copy the targets from another organization
Proceed with the technology choice, since the available technology determines the recovery objectives
Complete the BIA first, because recovery objectives come from business criticality
Choose the most expensive option to be safe
why: The BIA identifies what matters and how fast it must recover; technology choices follow. Cost-driven or borrowed targets are not tied to this organization's impact.

q: A ransomware attack encrypted production data and the backup repository because both shared the same administrator credentials. Which control would have MOST reduced the impact?
opts: More frequent full backups written to the same repository with the same credentials
Longer password expiry for administrators
Immutable backups stored separately from production credentials
Larger storage capacity for the repository
why: Immutable, logically separated backups survive credential compromise. Backing up more often to the same repository does not protect it, and password policy or capacity does not stop deletion.

q: A cloud application runs in a single availability zone. Which failure scenario is it MOST exposed to?
opts: A transient network error
An expired application certificate
Loss of the entire availability zone
Loss of a single virtual machine instance
why: Using one zone makes that facility a single point of failure. Individual instance loss could be handled by auto-scaling inside the zone and the others are unrelated to zone design.

q: A multi-region design must comply with a rule that customer data stays within one country. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Replicate to whichever region worldwide offers the cheapest storage and compute
Let the provider choose any region dynamically
Disable replication entirely
Choose recovery regions inside the permitted jurisdiction and verify replication
why: Resilience must respect residency rules, so recovery sites must be within the jurisdiction. Replicating anywhere violates the rule, no replication sacrifices availability and dynamic placement removes control.

q: Which statement about testing a disaster recovery plan is MOST accurate?
opts: A yearly review of the document is sufficient
A backup job that completes without error proves recovery will work
Testing is unnecessary for cloud workloads because the provider handles it
Only a restore or failover test shows whether the objectives can actually be met
why: Successful backups say nothing about restore success or timing. Document review does not test procedures, and the customer remains responsible for its own recovery.

q: Which TWO statements correctly relate recovery objectives to design? (Choose two.)
opts: RTO should always be set longer than the maximum tolerable downtime
A lower RTO requires more automation and standby capacity
A lower RTO can be met with weekly backups
RPO measures how long restoration takes
A lower RPO requires more frequent replication or backup
why: Tighter targets cost more. RPO measures data loss, not restoration time, and the RTO must fit within maximum tolerable downtime.

q: Which TWO risks are specifically associated with cloud adoption as seen in a cloud risk analysis? (Choose two.)
opts: Elimination of the need for patching customer-owned systems
Loss of governance and visibility over provider-operated layers
Guaranteed protection from regulatory penalties
Failure of isolation between tenants
why: Reduced control and shared-infrastructure isolation are core cloud-specific risks. Customer systems still need patching and regulatory duties remain.

q: The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable time to restore a service after an outage.
opts: True
False
why: That is the RTO. RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

q: Spreading workloads across availability zones protects against the failure of one data-center facility in a region.
opts: True
False
why: Zones are isolated failure domains within a region.

q: Asynchronous replication guarantees zero data loss during a site failure.
opts: True
False
why: Asynchronous replication can lose the most recent writes that had not yet been copied.

q: Recovery objectives for a system should be derived from the business impact analysis.
opts: True
False
why: The BIA ties recovery targets to business harm over time.

q: A regulated customer wants assurance that two network carriers serving a colocation site would both survive a single construction accident outside the building. Which design feature matters MOST?
opts: Both carriers terminate on the same patch panel, which simplifies management and cabling
Both carriers are chosen from the same parent company to simplify contracts and billing
The carriers' cables enter the building by physically separate routes
The carriers share one conduit into the building, which keeps installation costs low
why: Multi-vendor pathway connectivity only adds resilience when the paths are physically diverse. A shared conduit, a shared parent or a single termination point leaves one failure point.

q: A cloud workload is allowed to continue running during a planned power maintenance in the data center without any customer interruption. Which facility characteristic does this describe?
opts: Basic capacity with no redundant components, as in a Tier I design
A single power path with a generator that is tested yearly
Concurrent maintainability, as in a Tier III design
A design that tolerates failure only by shutting down the load
why: Concurrently maintainable sites can take components out of service without shutting down IT load. Tier I has no redundancy, and single paths or shutdown-based maintenance interrupt service.

q: A provider's site has two utility feeds, battery systems and generators, and every component has one spare available. Which description fits this redundancy level?
opts: A shared single feed with surge protection
2N with a fully duplicated independent path
N with no spare components
why: N+1 means the required capacity plus one spare component. 2N duplicates the entire path and N has no spare.

q: A company is deciding whether to build its own data center, lease colocation space or use public cloud regions for a new analytics platform that must be live in six weeks. Which factor argues MOST strongly against building?
opts: Public cloud prohibits the use of access control, so data requiring control must be hosted privately
Colocation space can never support encryption, so regulated data cannot be placed in it at all
Building always costs less than any other option once depreciation over twenty years is counted
The time and capital needed to construct and certify a facility exceed the deadline
why: Building takes long lead times and capital and requires proving controls to auditors. Colocation and cloud support encryption and access control, and building is rarely cheaper at small scale.

q: A cloud web application has a server-side request forgery flaw. An attacker uses it to query the workload's local metadata address and obtains temporary credentials for the instance role. Which mitigation reduces the impact MOST effectively?
opts: Move the application to a different availability zone so the attacker's request is routed elsewhere
Rotate the application's TLS certificate every day, which changes the identity but not the credentials stolen
Increase the instance size so the workload can absorb the larger number of malicious requests
Use the session-token version of the metadata service and give the role only the permissions it needs
why: Token-protected metadata access and least-privilege roles block both the request pattern and the blast radius. Instance size, zone placement and certificate rotation do not address credential theft through SSRF.

q: After an incident the team needs to prove which payload an attacker sent to a database server, but flow logs show only addresses and ports. What would have provided this evidence?
opts: A longer retention period for billing records and the cost allocation reports of the account
A larger number of availability zones for the application tier of the workload
Targeted packet capture through traffic mirroring on the affected segment
More frequent patching of the provider's management console and its client tools
why: Packet capture records content-level data that flow logs omit, and traffic mirroring supplies it in virtual networks. Billing retention, console patching and more zones do not capture payloads.

q: An architect must choose between sharing risk and transferring risk for a major outage of a critical vendor. Which action BEST represents risk sharing?
opts: Accepting the risk without a recorded decision, owner or review date for the residual exposure
Removing the workload from the business entirely, which is risk avoidance rather than sharing
Declining to assess the vendor at all, on the grounds that its certificate covers the risk
Contracting a second provider to carry part of the workload with a split of consequences
why: Sharing divides the impact with another party by contract or arrangement. Not assessing, removing the workload (avoidance) and silent acceptance are different or unsound treatments.

q: A BIA states that during recovery the order system needs only about half its normal capacity to keep the business viable. What does this requirement describe?
opts: Maximum tolerable downtime
Annualized rate of occurrence
Recovery point objective
Recovery service level
why: The recovery service level is the share of normal capacity required while recovering and allows a smaller recovery environment. RPO is about data loss, MTD is about time and ARO is a risk frequency.

q: A team wants to validate its disaster recovery procedures with minimal risk to production, but a document review alone has not exposed any issues. Which next test is MOST appropriate?
opts: Deleting the primary site in production to prove that the backup works under real conditions
No further testing, since a thorough document review proves that the procedures will work
A full interruption of production during business hours, to see whether the recovery procedures hold up
A tabletop exercise where participants walk through a realistic scenario
why: A tabletop is a low-risk step up in realism from a document review. A full interruption carries high risk and no testing leaves assumptions unproven.

q: A risk analyst values an application server at 200000, estimates that an outage would destroy 25 percent of that value and expects it twice a year. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
why: Single loss expectancy is 200000 times 0.25, giving 50000; multiplied by an annual rate of 2 the annualized loss expectancy is 100000. The other values come from missing one of the steps.

q: A cloud security team must show an auditor how an attacker moved from a stolen developer token to an object store. Which capability is MOST essential?
opts: Encryption of the finished audit report with a key held by the audit committee
Faster processors on the logging servers so that events are written to disk more quickly
Larger log retention on a single local disk attached to each of the application servers
Correlation of identity, management-plane and storage access logs across sources
why: Correlating events across identity, control-plane and data-plane logs reveals the chain of actions. Retention on one local disk, report encryption and processor speed do not link events.

q: Which TWO design choices improve the resilience of a cloud data center's environmental systems? (Choose two.)
opts: Clean-agent or pre-action fire suppression suited to equipment rooms
Redundant cooling units with monitored temperature sensors
Water-based sprinklers that discharge on every detector alarm
A single air conditioning unit shared by all halls
Locating the generator fuel supply in a single shared tank without monitoring
why: Cooling redundancy with monitoring and equipment-safe fire suppression protect continuity. A single cooling unit, indiscriminate water discharge and an unmonitored single fuel point create failure points.

q: Which TWO controls MOST directly protect the confidentiality of data traveling between workloads in different virtual networks? (Choose two.)
opts: A larger instance type for the sending workload
Mutual TLS between services
Disabling flow logs
An IPsec VPN or private link with encryption layered on top
A VLAN tag on the traffic
why: Encryption in transit, whether TLS or IPsec, protects confidentiality. VLAN tags only separate traffic and are not encryption, and instance size or logging settings do not encrypt.

q: Which TWO statements about qualitative and quantitative risk analysis are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: The two methods cannot be combined in one program
Qualitative analysis ranks risks on scales and is quicker but more subjective
Quantitative analysis supports cost-benefit decisions when reliable data exists
Qualitative analysis produces annualized loss expectancy in currency
Quantitative analysis never needs asset values
why: Quantitative uses values and probabilities for cost-benefit; qualitative uses ratings. Many programs combine them.

q: Two carriers entering a data center through the same trench give full protection against a single cable cut.
opts: True
False
why: Physical path diversity is required; carriers sharing one trench share a failure point.

q: The Uptime Institute Tier III classification describes a concurrently maintainable site.
opts: True
False
why: Tier III allows planned maintenance without shutting down IT load; Tier IV adds fault tolerance.

q: Annualized loss expectancy equals single loss expectancy multiplied by the annualized rate of occurrence.
opts: True
False
why: ALE = SLE x ARO; compare the reduction against the annual cost of the safeguard.

q: A VLAN encrypts traffic between its members.
opts: True
False
why: VLANs segment broadcast domains but provide no encryption; misconfigured trunks can even enable VLAN hopping.

q: A regional bank is choosing a site for a data center that must stay available through regional disasters. Which factor is MOST relevant to the decision?
opts: Whether the building was previously used for light industry rather than for ordinary office space
Proximity of the site to the bank's executive offices for easier ceremonial visits
Natural hazard exposure, diversity of power and carriers, and the legal jurisdiction of the site
The availability of the cheapest rack space regardless of utility diversity
why: Physical design is about hazard exposure, utilities, connectivity and jurisdiction, weighed with buy-or-build economics. Convenience and bargain space do not support resilience.

q: A provider hosts competing retailers on shared hosts. Which logical design measure MOST directly keeps their traffic and data apart?
opts: A single flat network where each retailer's workloads are told apart by naming conventions
Host firewalls configured identically on every host so that all tenants share the same rules and rule sets
One shared administrative account for all tenants, with tags to record who did what
Tenant-specific virtual networks, identities and keys with isolation enforced by policy
why: Tenant partitioning relies on separate networks, identities and keys enforced by the platform. Naming, shared accounts and uniform firewalls provide labels rather than isolation.

q: When utility power fails at a data center, which component carries the load during the seconds before the standby generators start and take over?
opts: A large fuel tank sized for several days of generator running
A surge protector on each rack's power strip
A power distribution unit that spreads the load across racks
An uninterruptible power supply using batteries or flywheels
why: An uninterruptible power supply bridges the gap until the generators reach speed and the transfer completes. A power distribution unit only distributes power, a surge protector only clamps spikes, and fuel keeps generators running but cannot supply power in the first seconds.

q: During risk assessment of a new cloud platform a team has listed its assets, the threats against them and the vulnerabilities present. What is the NEXT step in analysis?
opts: Transfer all identified risks to an insurer before they have been rated
Accept every risk that has a low purchase price for the corresponding safeguard
Estimate the likelihood and impact of each scenario to rate and rank the risks
Select the provider's default controls and treat the assessment as complete
why: Identification is followed by analysis of likelihood and impact, which supports ranking and treatment decisions. Accepting, transferring or defaulting before rating skips the reasoning that treatment depends on.

q: A customer database is snapshotted every six hours, but the business impact analysis allows at most fifteen minutes of data loss. Which change closes the gap?
opts: Add standby servers so that restoration takes less than fifteen minutes
Keep the six-hourly snapshots for ten years instead of ninety days
Replicate changes continuously or back up at least every fifteen minutes
Move the snapshots to a cheaper storage tier in the same region
why: Tolerable data loss is the recovery point objective, so recoverable copies must be no more than fifteen minutes apart. Standby servers shorten restoration time, longer retention only changes how far back a restore can go, and a cheaper tier lowers cost without improving the recovery point.

q: Auditors reconstructing an incident across several cloud accounts find that events from different services appear in impossible orders. Which fix addresses the root cause?
opts: Encrypt the logs in transit to the central collector using mutually authenticated TLS
Synchronize every system to a trusted time source and log timestamps in UTC
Turn on debug-level logging in every service so that more detail is recorded
Extend log retention from ninety days to one year so that the events can be sorted out later
why: Correlation depends on consistent time, and unsynchronized clocks or mixed time zones make the event order unreliable. Longer retention, transport encryption and more verbose logging do not correct timestamps.

q: A cloud customer using IaaS remains responsible for physical access controls at the provider's data center.
opts: True
False
why: Physical and environmental protection of the facility is the provider's duty; the customer verifies it through audit reports and contracts.

q: A team discovers an authorization design flaw one week before launch that requires reworking the data model. In which activity would this flaw MOST cost-effectively have been found?
opts: A yearly security awareness course
Threat modeling during design
Penetration testing after deployment
Production monitoring after launch
why: Threat modeling at design time finds structural flaws when they are cheapest to fix. Testing after deployment and monitoring find them late, and awareness training does not review a design.

q: A threat model shows that an attacker could send a request pretending to be another user to reach private records. Which STRIDE category does this describe?
opts: Spoofing
Denial of service
Tampering
Repudiation
why: Impersonating an identity is spoofing. Tampering alters data, repudiation denies actions without evidence and denial of service degrades availability.

q: A company needs to find vulnerable open-source libraries and the exact versions in each release so it can respond quickly to a new advisory. Which approach BEST achieves this?
opts: A web application firewall in front of the application
Static analysis of only the company's own source code before each release
Software composition analysis with a maintained software bill of materials
A quarterly code review by a senior developer
why: SCA and an SBOM inventory third-party components. SAST of in-house code misses libraries, a WAF is a runtime filter and manual reviews cannot track dependency versions at scale.

q: Which testing technique can find a misconfigured response header and an exploitable input path in a running staging environment WITHOUT access to the source code?
opts: Peer code review
Software composition analysis
Static application security testing of the source code
Dynamic application security testing
why: DAST probes the running application from outside. SAST and review need source, and SCA examines components rather than behavior.

q: An API returns another customer's invoice when a user changes the invoice number in the request, though authentication succeeded. Which problem is this?
opts: Missing rate limiting
Weak transport encryption
Broken object-level authorization
Insufficient logging and monitoring of API activity
why: Authentication proved who the caller is, but the API failed to check whether they may access that object. This is the leading API risk. Logging, encryption and rate limiting are separate gaps.

q: A company's build server was compromised and attackers inserted a backdoor into released software, even though the source repository was clean. Which control would have MOST helped detect or prevent this?
opts: A WAF rule update for the production site
Encrypting the source repository at rest
Signed build artifacts with provenance verification before deployment
More frequent manual testing of the final application before release
why: Provenance and signing show that an artifact came from the trusted pipeline and was not altered. Manual testing may miss a backdoor, a WAF does not examine build integrity and encrypting a clean repository does nothing for the build system.

q: A customer support chatbot built on a large language model retrieves web pages to answer questions. A page contains hidden text telling the model to email customer records to an outside address. Which defense is MOST effective?
opts: Increase the model's temperature setting
Move the chatbot to a larger instance size
Add the instruction 'ignore malicious text' to the system prompt as the only control
Treat retrieved content as untrusted and limit the model's tool permissions
why: Indirect prompt injection is mitigated by least privilege on tools, output controls and treating inputs as untrusted. A system prompt instruction alone can be overridden, and temperature or instance size are unrelated.

q: Which statement about a web application firewall is MOST accurate?
opts: It encrypts data stored in the application database
It removes the need to patch application code because attacks never reach the server
It authenticates users to the application
A compensating control that reduces exposure while the code flaw is fixed
why: A WAF filters known attack patterns but does not remove vulnerabilities. It does not provide storage encryption or authentication.

q: A security team wants developers to receive vulnerability feedback in their code editor and pull requests before merging. Which practice BEST supports this?
opts: Shift-left automated scanning integrated into the build pipeline
Annual penetration tests by an external firm
Monitoring production logs for exceptions
A security sign-off meeting held by the review board after release
why: Automated scanning in the pipeline gives fast feedback early. Annual tests and post-release meetings are too late and log monitoring is detective only.

q: Which action BEST reduces the risk that a query to a deployed machine learning model reveals whether a particular person's record was in its training data?
opts: Increase the size of the training data without changing the training process
Limit query rates and output detail, and use privacy-preserving training
Store the model in a bucket with a long, random name
Publish the model weights so researchers can inspect them
why: Inference attacks rely on repeated, detailed queries; limiting them and training with privacy protections reduces leakage. Publishing weights makes it easier and obscure names are not access control.

q: A cloud-hosted service is vulnerable to SQL injection. Which fix addresses the ROOT cause?
opts: Encrypt the database connection with TLS
Block the attacker's current source IP address
Use parameterized queries and validate input against an allow-list
Increase the size of the database instance to absorb malicious queries
why: Parameterized queries stop input from being interpreted as code. Blocking an address is temporary, TLS protects transit and size is unrelated.

q: Which TWO practices strengthen API security? (Choose two.)
opts: Validate requests against a defined schema and enforce rate limits
Disable logging to protect user privacy
Use a single shared key embedded in all mobile apps
Rely on obscure URL paths to hide endpoints
Authorize each request against the specific object and action
why: Per-request authorization and input and rate controls are core. Obscurity, shared embedded keys and no logging weaken security.

q: Which TWO are valid reasons to combine static and dynamic testing in a pipeline? (Choose two.)
opts: Either one alone finds every class of vulnerability
Dynamic testing finds runtime and configuration issues static tools miss
Static analysis can detect flaws in the provider's hypervisor
Static analysis finds code flaws early without a running system
Dynamic testing requires access to the source code
why: The techniques are complementary. Neither finds everything, DAST does not need source and SAST examines customer code only.

q: OWASP Top 10 is a certification standard that applications must pass to be considered secure.
opts: True
False
why: It is an awareness list of common risk categories, not a certifiable standard.

q: Threat modeling is most valuable when performed during design, before code is written.
opts: True
False
why: Design-time modeling finds structural flaws cheaply.

q: A software bill of materials helps identify which applications contain a newly announced vulnerable library.
opts: True
False
why: An SBOM inventories components so exposure can be assessed quickly.

q: Penetration testing of a cloud provider's shared infrastructure by a customer is allowed without notification.
opts: True
False
why: Testing must follow the provider's published rules; shared infrastructure is generally off limits.

q: Output from a large language model should be treated as untrusted input by downstream systems.
opts: True
False
why: Model output can contain injected or incorrect content, so it must be validated like any external input.

q: An organization wants employees to sign in once to access many SaaS applications and have access removed everywhere when they leave. Which approach BEST meets this?
opts: A shared password stored in a team document
Federated single sign-on with automated provisioning and deprovisioning
Separate local accounts in each application, managed individually by the application owners
A spreadsheet of accounts reviewed once a year
why: Federation centralizes authentication and, with provisioning, makes leaver removal consistent. Shared passwords and separate accounts create orphaned access and spreadsheets are slow and error-prone.

q: A mobile application needs permission to read a user's calendar from a third-party service without ever seeing the user's password. Which protocol is designed for this?
opts: OAuth 2.0
SAML assertions for web single sign-on
Basic authentication over TLS
Kerberos ticket granting
why: OAuth 2.0 delegates limited access using tokens. SAML is enterprise web sign-on, basic authentication exposes the password to the app and Kerberos is for enterprise network authentication.

q: A developer states that because their application uses OAuth 2.0 tokens, it already authenticates users. What is the MOST accurate response?
opts: OpenID Connect replaces TLS
OAuth handles authorization; OpenID Connect adds the authentication layer
OAuth is purely an authentication protocol
SAML is required for any form of token-based authentication in cloud services
why: OAuth was designed for delegated authorization; identity is added by OpenID Connect. The other statements misdescribe the protocols.

q: Cloud administrators hold permanent elevated roles even though they use them only a few times a month. Which change MOST reduces risk?
opts: Longer passwords with stricter complexity for administrator accounts
Just-in-time elevation with approval and session recording
Moving administrators to a separate office
Renaming administrator accounts
why: Removing standing privilege shrinks the exposure window and adds accountability. Longer passwords help but leave permanent privilege, and the other options do not.

q: A pipeline uses a long-lived access key stored in a repository to deploy infrastructure. Which approach is BEST?
opts: Share the key with the whole engineering team
Encode the key in base64 before committing it
Rotate the key once per year but keep it stored in the shared code repository for the team
Use a platform-issued short-lived workload identity with scoped permissions
why: Short-lived, scoped credentials issued to the workload remove stored secrets. Yearly rotation leaves a long exposure, sharing widens it and encoding is not protection.

q: A company must grant access based on department, data sensitivity, device compliance and time of day. Which model fits BEST?
opts: Attribute-based access control
Role-based access control only
Discretionary access control by file owners
Mandatory access control with fixed labels only
why: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes and context at decision time. Role-only models cannot express context, DAC leaves decisions to owners and fixed labels lack contextual factors.

q: Employees use unsanctioned file-sharing services to send work documents. The company wants visibility and policy enforcement over these cloud services. Which tool BEST helps?
opts: A hardware security module
A network time server
A cloud access security broker
A load balancer
why: A CASB discovers cloud service usage and enforces data and access policy. An HSM stores keys, a time server synchronizes clocks and a load balancer distributes traffic.

q: Which authentication approach is MOST resistant to phishing for a cloud administrator?
opts: A long password that is subject to a strict complexity and rotation policy
A security question
A hardware security key or passkey bound to the legitimate site
A one-time code sent by SMS
why: Hardware keys and passkeys verify the site and cannot be relayed easily. SMS codes can be intercepted or phished, passwords can be disclosed and questions are guessable.

q: Which TWO statements about federated identity are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Compromise of the identity provider can affect many connected services
Federation only works inside one organization
The relying service trusts signed assertions from the identity provider
Federation removes the need for authorization decisions
Each service must store a separate copy of the user's password
why: Trust is based on signed assertions, and centralization concentrates risk. Services do not store the passwords, authorization is still needed and federation spans organizations.

q: SMS one-time codes are the strongest form of multi-factor authentication available.
opts: True
False
why: SMS can be intercepted or socially engineered; hardware keys and passkeys are stronger.

q: Separation of duties means one person should not be able to both request and approve a sensitive action.
opts: True
False
why: Splitting critical tasks prevents any single person from completing fraud or abuse alone.

q: Orphaned accounts of departed employees are reduced by automating provisioning and deprovisioning.
opts: True
False
why: Automation ties account removal to HR events rather than manual follow-up.

q: A product team wants security requirements that can be verified in testing and that scale with the sensitivity of each application, from low-risk internal tools to payment services. Which resource is MOST appropriate as the basis?
opts: A list of programming languages approved by the architects and the versions of each they allow
A single penetration test report from last year
The OWASP Top 10 used as a pass or fail certificate
The OWASP Application Security Verification Standard with its assurance levels
why: ASVS provides testable requirements at graduated levels. The Top 10 is an awareness list rather than a standard to certify against, an old test report is not a requirement set and a language list does not define security.

q: A developer team is building a customer-facing assistant on a generative AI model that can call internal tools and wants a published risk list tailored to this kind of system. Which source is MOST relevant?
opts: The OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
A generic list of network ports and the services that traditionally use each of them on servers
The CWE Top 25 alone, because it is the only list that ranks weaknesses by severity
The OWASP Top 10 for web applications alone, since it already covers every application type
why: The LLM list covers prompt injection, excessive agency, output handling and model poisoning that general web lists omit. The web Top 10 and CWE list are useful but not tailored, and port lists are unrelated.

q: A new feature lets a user reset a password. In design review a security engineer proposes a list of ways an attacker could misuse it: enumerating accounts, flooding the endpoint and replaying a token. What is this technique?
opts: Abuse case analysis feeding negative tests
Software composition analysis of dependencies
Functional regression testing of the happy path
Capacity planning for the endpoint
why: Abuse cases describe malicious use and become negative tests. Happy-path regression checks intended behavior, capacity planning concerns load and composition analysis inspects libraries.

q: A threat model produced a long list of threats categorized with STRIDE. The team now needs to rank them so the highest risks are fixed first. Which scoring model is named in the outline for this purpose?
opts: PASTA
SAFECode
ATASM
DREAD
why: DREAD scores damage, reproducibility, exploitability, affected users and discoverability. PASTA and ATASM are modeling methods and SAFECode is a body of practice guidance.

q: An organization wants a threat modeling approach tied to business objectives that simulates attacker behavior in several defined stages. Which method fits BEST?
opts: CVSS
PASTA
DREAD
STRIDE
why: PASTA is a seven-stage, risk-centric process linking business goals to attack simulation. DREAD and CVSS score threats or vulnerabilities and STRIDE categorizes threat types.

q: A team sees that its code scanner flags a library problem in release 4.2, but the release cannot be reproduced because the configuration and dependency versions were edited by hand on a server. Which practice would have prevented this?
opts: Software configuration management with version control and tagged, reproducible builds
Disabling the code scanner for older releases so that only new releases generate findings
Giving every developer root access to production so that fixes can be applied directly on servers
Moving the application to a larger virtual machine
why: Version-controlled code, configuration and dependencies make any build reproducible and traceable. Turning off scanning, sizing up and widening access make things worse.

q: A team can see the source code of a SaaS integration and tests its logic for injection flaws without running it. Which testing category is this?
opts: White-box testing using static analysis
Load testing for performance
Black-box testing using fuzzing
Gray-box testing without code access
why: Inspecting source without running it is static, white-box testing. Fuzzing runs the program from outside, gray-box testing has partial knowledge and load testing is non-functional performance work.

q: A company relies on an open-source library that a single maintainer abandoned, with a license that requires publishing derived source. What is the MOST appropriate response?
opts: Allow each team to pull whichever copy of the library it prefers from public sources
Review license obligations and maintainer health, then replace or fork under a managed process
Keep using it unchanged, because open-source software carries no license or maintenance obligations for the user
Remove all versioning information to avoid disclosure
why: Open-source intake includes license review and health assessment, with a plan to replace or maintain. Ignoring obligations, hiding version data and unrestricted downloads increase risk.

q: A deployment manifest references a container image only by the tag latest. An attacker with push rights to the registry overwrites that tag with a modified image, and the next rollout pulls it. Which practice BEST prevents this?
opts: Reference images by immutable digest and enable tag immutability in the registry
Rotate the registry's TLS certificate every week and require TLS 1.3 for all pulls
Add registry replicas in other regions so that pulls keep working during an outage
Scan the image once at build time and then trust the tag from that point on
why: A digest identifies the exact image content and an immutable tag cannot be silently overwritten, so a rollout pulls only what was reviewed. A one-time scan does not stop the tag being replaced later, certificate rotation does not authenticate content, and replicas improve availability only.

q: A legacy partner sends large XML messages to a cloud service, and a malformed message with an external entity reference crashed a parser last month. Which component would BEST filter such traffic before it reaches the application?
opts: A hardware security module that protects the signing keys
A database activity monitor that records privileged queries
An XML firewall that validates schemas and blocks malformed messages
A content delivery cache that serves partner responses from the edge
why: XML firewalls inspect and validate XML and SOAP traffic. HSMs protect keys, activity monitors watch database queries and caches speed delivery.

q: A company exposes many internal services as APIs and wants one place to authenticate callers, rate limit and log requests, while each service still checks authorization for its own objects. Which component fits?
opts: A honeypot that lures attackers away from production
An API gateway in front of the services
A file integrity monitor on each service host
A bastion host for administrator access
why: A gateway centralizes authentication, throttling and logging at the edge. File integrity monitors, bastions and honeypots do not serve API traffic.

q: A team needs to open email attachments from unknown senders to check for malware in the cloud, without any risk to production systems. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Detonate them in an isolated sandbox with no route to production
Disable antivirus on a shared server so that the files cannot be quarantined during the test
Copy them to the production file share first
Open them on a developer's laptop, which has VPN access and a current antivirus tool
why: Sandboxes isolate untrusted content with restricted permissions and network access. The other choices expose real systems.

q: A SaaS application trusts sign-in assertions from an external identity provider. The provider's signing key is stolen. What is the MOST significant consequence?
opts: Application logs begin to delete themselves automatically, hiding the signs of earlier logins
Only the provider's public marketing site is affected, because assertions never reach other applications
Users must pick much longer passwords for every federated application to stay safe
An attacker can forge assertions and sign in as any user across the federated applications
why: Federation trusts the signed assertion, so a stolen signing key lets an attacker impersonate anyone in every relying application. The other outcomes are unrelated.

q: A development team in a regulated company wants to avoid a single failure where both the code review and the build approval are done by the same person. Which principle does this support?
opts: Loose coupling of services across the pipeline
Role stacking to make the pipeline more efficient
Separation of duties in the delivery pipeline
Security through obscurity of the pipeline
why: Separating review from approval prevents one person from pushing unreviewed changes. Obscurity, loose coupling and stacking roles do not provide that control.

q: Which TWO statements about functional and non-functional testing are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Functional testing is the only type that can run in a pipeline
Security, performance and availability testing are non-functional
Security testing is outside the testing lifecycle
A feature can pass every functional test and still be exploitable
Non-functional testing checks only that features match the requirement document
why: Functional testing checks behavior against requirements; security and other qualities are non-functional and both can be automated in pipelines.

q: Which TWO measures help secure a continuous integration and delivery pipeline? (Choose two.)
opts: A single long-lived administrator key shared by all jobs
Allowing build agents to reach any internal network without restriction
Protected branches with required reviews and signed artifacts
Storing secrets in the repository for easy access
Short-lived credentials with least privilege for build jobs
why: Least-privilege short-lived credentials and protected, signed delivery limit what a compromise can do. Shared administrator keys, unrestricted agents and committed secrets are classic pipeline failures.

q: Which THREE belong in third-party software management? (Choose three.)
opts: Trusting any package with many downloads without verification
An inventory of every external component and service
Letting each developer decide silently which components to use
Tracking of vulnerabilities with a plan for replacement or patches
Vendor and license review before adoption
why: Inventory, vendor and license review and vulnerability tracking are the foundation. Popularity is not verification and ad hoc decisions create blind spots.

q: In the OWASP Top 10:2025, broken access control is still listed first.
opts: True
False
why: The 2025 edition keeps broken access control at number one and adds categories for supply chain failures and mishandling of exceptional conditions.

q: The ASVS is a certification that an application passes once and keeps permanently.
opts: True
False
why: ASVS is a requirements and verification standard with levels; it is applied per application and revisited as the application changes.

q: A white-box test requires access to the source code or design of the application.
opts: True
False
why: White-box testers have internal knowledge; black-box testers have none and gray-box testers have partial knowledge.

q: An API gateway removes the need for each service to perform its own authorization checks.
opts: True
False
why: The gateway enforces edge policy, but object-level authorization must still be checked by the service.

q: Signed build provenance helps detect that an artifact was not produced by the expected pipeline.
opts: True
False
why: Signature and provenance verification address integrity and authenticity in the supply chain.

q: Compromise of a federated identity provider's signing key affects only one application.
opts: True
False
why: Every relying application that trusts the provider's signature is exposed.

q: A team moving from waterfall to agile worries that end-of-project security reviews will block each sprint. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Put security requirements, threat modeling and automated tests in every iteration and in the definition of done
Skip threat modeling entirely because agile teams prefer working software over analysis
Ask the security team to approve every user story before the sprint can start
Keep a single security review after the final sprint and treat all earlier work as draft
why: Agile needs security tasks inside each iteration and acceptance criteria, rather than a late gate. A single late review finds problems too late, and per-story approvals do not scale.

q: A profile-update API copies every field in the submitted JSON onto the stored user record, so an ordinary user who adds an extra role field set to administrator becomes an administrator. Which OWASP API Security Top 10 risk is this?
opts: Broken object property level authorization
Unrestricted resource consumption of the profile service
Improper inventory management of retired API versions
Security misconfiguration of the web server headers
why: The API lets the caller write a property they are not allowed to change, which is broken object property level authorization (mass assignment). The other risks involve load, configuration or old versions.

q: The CWE Top 25 ranks the most dangerous software weakness types using vulnerability data, and it complements the OWASP Top 10 rather than replacing it.
opts: True
False
why: It lists weakness classes by prevalence and severity, while the OWASP list is an awareness document of web application risk categories.

q: A customer's regulated workload runs on shared cloud hardware, and the compliance officer worries about the provider's own administrators. Which treatment fits the cloud-specific risk BEST?
opts: Store the encryption keys in the same account as the data for convenience of recovery
Move the workload to a larger instance type that is harder for administrators to see
Use customer-held keys, restrict and log provider access and review the provider's insider controls
Accept the risk because provider staff are certified and therefore cannot access any customer data
why: Customer-held keys, logged access and assurance about provider controls reduce provider insider exposure. Certification does not prevent access, instance size does not hide data and co-locating keys with data weakens separation.

q: A QA team's functional tests all pass, yet a user can bypass a payment step by replaying an earlier request. Which testing gap does this reveal?
opts: Compatibility testing was missing, because older browsers do not enforce payment steps
Usability testing was missing, because replay depends on a confusing interface
Load testing was missing, because replay attacks only occur under heavy traffic
Abuse case testing was missing, because functional tests only confirm intended behavior
why: Abuse and misuse cases deliberately try to break rules the way an attacker would, while functional tests confirm that expected paths work. The other test types do not look for deliberate bypass.

q: During QA test runs a team wants security findings tied to the exact line of code that handled the request, found by instrumenting the running application. Which technique fits?
opts: Interactive application security testing
Static application security testing alone, because it executes the application in production
Software composition analysis, because it reports where tainted data flows at runtime
A tabletop exercise, because it traces requests through the compiled application
why: IAST instruments a running application and reports vulnerabilities with code context. SAST analyzes code without running it, SCA inventories components and a tabletop is a discussion.

q: A cloud account is suspected to be compromised, but the team finds the management-plane audit trail was never enabled. What is the MOST significant consequence?
opts: All data in the account is automatically encrypted
The attacker's activity is automatically blocked
They cannot reliably reconstruct which identities made which changes
The provider will refuse to restore the account until a ticket has been opened
why: Management-plane logging records who did what through the console and APIs; without it, reconstruction is guesswork. The other outcomes do not follow from missing logs.

q: During an incident an engineer wants to power off a compromised virtual machine immediately. What should the team do FIRST to preserve evidence while limiting spread?
opts: Terminate the instance immediately so the attacker loses access to the host
Delete the instance's logs to avoid confusion
Reboot the instance to clear malicious processes
Isolate the instance and snapshot its disks and memory before it is changed
why: Isolation contains spread and snapshots preserve evidence. Terminating or rebooting destroys volatile evidence, and deleting logs destroys what is needed.

q: A team collected disk images from a compromised server but did not record who handled them. What is the MOST significant problem?
opts: The broken chain of custody may make the evidence inadmissible
The images cannot be compressed
The images will fail to boot on a standard forensic analysis workstation
The images cannot be hashed
why: Chain of custody documents handling and proves integrity. The other concerns are technical details unrelated to admissibility.

q: Which item should be collected FIRST in a live cloud forensic investigation, according to the order of volatility?
opts: Printed network diagrams stored in the facility
Archived backup media held at an offsite storage facility
Memory contents and running process information
Remote log archives held in a central collection service
why: Memory is the most volatile and is lost on stop or reboot. Backups and archived logs persist, and diagrams are documentation.

q: A company runs workloads in three cloud providers and each provider's logs use a different format, so analysts miss related alerts. Which action BEST improves detection?
opts: Have analysts log in to each provider's console daily
Centralize logs in a SIEM with a normalized schema and consistent identity data
Rely only on each provider's built-in alerts
Disable logging in the two providers whose log formats are the hardest to parse
why: Normalization and centralization enable correlation across providers. Manual review does not scale, disabling logs removes visibility and separate alerts miss cross-cloud patterns.

q: An alert shows a developer's credentials were used from two continents within ten minutes. What is the BEST immediate response?
opts: Revoke sessions and keys, require MFA again and investigate activity
Change the developer's job title in the directory
Wait for a second alert to confirm the pattern
Reduce log retention to lower storage costs while the investigation proceeds
why: Impossible travel indicates likely credential compromise; contain first by revoking access, then investigate. Waiting prolongs exposure and the other options do not address the risk.

q: A security operations lead wants to reduce time to respond for a well-understood, low-risk alert that currently needs manual steps. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
opts: Replace the SIEM with a larger one
Require every alert of this type to be escalated to the executive team for approval
Ignore this alert type
Automate the playbook with SOAR and keep analyst approval for high-impact actions
why: SOAR automation speeds repeatable steps while keeping humans on risky decisions. A bigger SIEM does not automate response, ignoring alerts removes control and escalating everything overwhelms leadership.

q: Which activity is the cloud customer's responsibility for a virtual machine running in IaaS?
opts: Updating the provider's storage firmware
Patching the guest operating system
Maintaining the provider's physical data center
Patching the hypervisor
why: In IaaS the customer manages everything above the virtualization layer. The other tasks belong to the provider.

q: An engineer restored a failed service by editing a production server directly, outside the normal change process. Which follow-up BEST keeps change control intact?
opts: Leave it undocumented because emergency changes are exempt from change management
Require a full change board meeting before any future fix, even while a service is down
Record it as an emergency change, review it afterwards and fold a valid fix into the baseline and templates
Roll the server back to the baseline at once, even if the failure returns
why: Emergency changes are expedited, not exempt: they are recorded, reviewed afterwards and, if valid, built into the baseline so the system does not drift. Skipping the record breaks accountability, demanding a full board during an outage defeats the purpose of the emergency path, and a blind rollback restores the failure.

q: A machine learning model that approves transactions begins behaving differently without any approved update, and recent training data included unreviewed external sources. How should the security team treat this?
opts: As a licensing issue for the vendor to resolve
As normal variation that needs no action
As evidence that one of the provider's data centers has suffered a hardware failure
As a potential security incident involving tampering or poisoning, to be investigated
why: Unexplained model change can indicate poisoning or tampering. Ignoring it risks fraud, and neither data center failure nor licensing explains it.

q: Which statement about incident response in the cloud is MOST accurate?
opts: The provider alone investigates all incidents on the customer's behalf, so the customer needs no readiness of its own
Incident response should begin only after the provider has formally confirmed that a breach occurred
Logs from ephemeral resources can always be recovered from the provider later, even if logging was never enabled
Preparation, including logging and provider contacts, must be done before an incident because evidence may be ephemeral
why: Because resources are ephemeral and access depends on contracts, readiness comes first. The provider does not run the customer's response, waiting for its confirmation delays containment, and logs not collected may be gone.

q: A regulator will be notified of a breach affecting customers. Who should decide the exact content and timing of the external statement?
opts: The on-call engineer who found the issue and has the most technical detail
The cloud provider's help desk
The marketing team alone
Legal and compliance leadership with incident command input
why: Disclosure carries legal obligations, so legal and compliance lead with technical facts from the response team. Single engineers or marketing lack the authority and providers do not speak for the customer.

q: Which control gives continuous detection of publicly exposed storage and unencrypted databases across many cloud accounts?
opts: A tape backup system for archival data
A VPN gateway
A hardware security module
Cloud security posture management
why: CSPM continuously evaluates configuration against policy. An HSM, VPN gateway and tape backups do not assess configuration.

q: A team monitors alert counts and reports that more alerts means better security. What is the BEST critique?
opts: Fewer logs always mean better security
Metrics should never be reported to leadership because they cause unnecessary concern
Volume does not measure effectiveness; time to detect and respond does
Alert counts are the only valid metric
why: Effectiveness is shown by outcomes such as detection and response times. Counts alone may reflect noise, and metrics support leadership oversight.

q: Which TWO actions improve the integrity of logs used for investigations? (Choose two.)
opts: Synchronize clocks across systems
Delete old logs weekly to save cost
Allow administrators to edit entries freely
Store logs only on the system that produced them
Forward logs to a central store the source system cannot modify
why: Central tamper-resistant storage and consistent time make logs trustworthy. Local-only logs and editable entries can be altered, and weekly deletion destroys evidence.

q: Which TWO are typical challenges of forensics in the cloud? (Choose two.)
opts: All evidence is stored on the customer's laptop
Customers always have physical access to the servers
Multi-tenancy never affects evidence handling
Access to underlying hardware and some logs depends on the provider
Ephemeral resources may disappear before evidence is collected
why: Short-lived resources and provider-held evidence limit collection. Customers do not have physical access, and multi-tenancy complicates evidence handling.

q: Which THREE are sound preparation activities for cloud incident response? (Choose three.)
opts: Wait until an incident to decide who is in charge
Enable and centralize management-plane and workload logging
Agree evidence and escalation procedures with the provider
Set up a pre-approved isolated account for forensic analysis
Disable alerts to reduce noise before audits
why: Logging, an isolated analysis environment and agreed provider processes are preparation. Improvising authority and disabling alerts are not.

q: Which TWO inputs belong to threat hunting rather than reactive alert triage? (Choose two.)
opts: Closing a ticket generated by a known false positive
A hypothesis that an attacker is abusing a particular cloud role
Applying a vendor patch announced last month
Searching across logs for unusual behavior not tied to any alert
why: Hunting is proactive, hypothesis-driven searching. Closing known alerts and patching are routine operations.

q: Terminating a compromised cloud instance is always the best first step because it ends the attacker's access.
opts: True
False
why: Isolate and capture evidence first; termination destroys volatile data and may lose the instance entirely.

q: A SIEM is only useful if logs from relevant systems are collected and time-synchronized.
opts: True
False
why: Correlation depends on complete and consistently timed data.

q: Change management applies only to production application code, not infrastructure configuration.
opts: True
False
why: Infrastructure and configuration changes carry risk and need controlled review and recording as well.

q: The customer is responsible for patching the hypervisor in an IaaS service.
opts: True
False
why: The provider operates and patches the hypervisor; the customer patches guest systems.

q: A documented chain of custody helps show that digital evidence has not been altered.
opts: True
False
why: It records every handling step from collection to presentation.

q: Machine learning can assist threat hunting by highlighting anomalous behavior across large volumes of logs.
opts: True
False
why: ML helps identify patterns humans would miss, though results still need analyst validation.

q: A cloud incident response plan can be developed after an incident because cloud providers keep all logs indefinitely.
opts: True
False
why: Providers retain logs only to their stated policies; customers must configure and retain their own.

q: Persistent drift between running systems and the approved baseline is a security concern even if the systems work.
opts: True
False
why: Unreviewed change can open vulnerabilities and complicates investigations.

q: Forensic readiness means collecting evidence only after an incident has been confirmed by the regulator.
opts: True
False
why: It means preparing logging, tools and agreements in advance so evidence is available when needed.

q: A new virtual machine image template exposes remote desktop and secure shell ports to the internet, has a default administrator password and logging disabled. Which principle was MOST clearly ignored?
opts: Elastic scaling of resources
Secure by default configuration
Broad network access for customers
Resource pooling among tenants
why: Safe initial settings (closed ports, no default credentials, logging on) define secure by default. Elasticity, pooling and broad access are cloud characteristics, not configuration principles.

q: Administrators in a cloud environment need to manage servers in private subnets. Which design BEST limits exposure?
opts: Public addresses on every server, protected only by strong passwords that are changed each quarter
Open inbound access from the whole internet to the management port
A single shared administrator account protected by a very long password stored in a team vault
A hardened bastion with multi-factor authentication and recorded sessions as the only entry point
why: A controlled jump point reduces exposed surface and adds accountability. Public addresses, shared accounts and open ports increase attack surface.

q: A hypervisor cluster must apply a firmware patch to one host without causing downtime for hosted applications. Which operational feature makes this possible?
opts: Powering off the host immediately and restarting the guests once the update has finished
Deleting the guest virtual machines and rebuilding them from templates after the update
Disabling monitoring on the cluster so that the update does not trigger alerts and tickets
Placing the host in maintenance mode so workloads migrate to other hosts first
why: Maintenance mode evacuates workloads before servicing, relying on cluster capacity. Powering off, disabling monitoring and deleting guests cause avoidable outage or blindness.

q: A cluster's high availability configuration restarts virtual machines on surviving hosts after a node failure, but during a test several machines failed to restart. What is the MOST likely design flaw?
opts: Insufficient reserved failover capacity on the remaining hosts
The virtual machines were too small to run their applications once the host recovered
The network used a VLAN
The hosts used encrypted storage, which prevents guests from being restarted on another host
why: High availability needs spare capacity to absorb failed hosts' workloads. Encryption, small guests or VLANs do not prevent restarts.

q: A monitoring dashboard shows one host's fan speed dropping and temperature rising. What is the BEST response?
opts: Turn off hardware alerts for the whole fleet to reduce noise and operator fatigue
Raise the host's utilization to burn off the heat in the processor and the fans
Wait until the host crashes to confirm the problem and then rebuild it from a template
Migrate workloads away and repair the hardware before it fails
why: Hardware monitoring exists to act before failure. Waiting, silencing alerts and increasing load make failure more likely.

q: A team sees a sudden, sustained rise in compute usage in an account at night with no deployment scheduled. Which interpretation deserves FIRST attention?
opts: A sign that the provider's service level has improved and fewer instances are needed
Possible abuse such as cryptomining through stolen credentials
Normal behavior of a scheduled change nobody recorded
A routine seasonal backup of the monitoring software
why: Unexplained sustained usage is a classic abuse indicator and should be investigated. The other explanations ignore the absence of a recorded change.

q: A security lead wants operating systems to stay in a known good state: documented settings, automated detection of deviations and prompt correction. Which cycle describes this?
opts: Allow administrators to change settings freely whenever an application owner requests it
Patch only after an incident has shown that a weakness is exploited
Baseline, monitor and remediate against an approved configuration
Deploy once and archive the image, since a deployed system should never change
why: Hardening is maintained by baselining, monitoring drift and remediating. One-time deployment, reactive patching and free changes allow drift.

q: An organization wants a certifiable standard it can use to demonstrate a formal IT service management system, covering incident, change and service level processes. Which should it choose?
opts: COBIT 2019
ISO/IEC 20000-1
CIS Critical Security Controls
ISO/IEC 27001
why: ISO/IEC 20000-1 specifies a service management system. ISO/IEC 27001 certifies an information security management system, COBIT is a governance framework and CIS Controls are prioritized safeguards.

q: A board wants one framework to organize cybersecurity outcomes around govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover. Which is it?
opts: The COSO internal control framework
ITIL 4
PCI DSS
NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
why: CSF 2.0 organizes outcomes into those six functions, including the new Govern function. ITIL, PCI DSS and COSO have different structures and purposes.

q: A small company with limited staff wants a prioritized set of safeguards that scales to its size, starting with essential hygiene. Which resource fits BEST?
opts: A COBIT governance design built for a multinational with a large internal audit team
CIS Critical Security Controls using implementation groups
The full catalog of the NIST SP 800-53 high baseline applied to every system
A PCI DSS assessment covering all company data, not only payment card data
why: CIS Controls implementation groups let smaller organizations start with essential safeguards. A high baseline catalog, an enterprise governance design and a payment assessment are not sized or targeted for that goal.

q: A cloud provider needs to tell customers about a maintenance window and a security incident affecting several tenants. Which preparation BEST ensures consistent and timely communication?
opts: Posting only on social media after the incident has already been reported in the press
Sending nothing to anyone until a regulator or a customer requests an explanation
Letting each engineer email affected customers individually with whatever details he or she has
Predefined stakeholder lists, channels and approved templates with named owners
why: Planned channels, owners and approved wording make communication timely and consistent. Ad hoc emails, delayed posts and silence create legal and trust failures.

q: Service restoration for a failing application succeeded within ten minutes, but the same failure recurred three times that week. Which ITIL-style process should now take over?
opts: Capacity management, which plans resources and removes unused storage after the incident
Continuity management, which would relocate the data center to a different region
Release management, which ships more features in each release cycle
Problem management to find and remove the root cause
why: Problem management addresses underlying causes of recurring incidents. Release, capacity and continuity management are separate processes.

q: An investigator must collect evidence from a compromised workload and a cloud storage service whose provider logs sit outside the customer's control. Which preparation would have helped MOST?
opts: A policy that evidence is gathered only after the incident is closed and approved by management
Pre-agreed forensic procedures and log access arrangements in the contract
A verbal promise from the provider's staff to retain all logs informally for as long as needed
Disabling logging in the affected accounts to avoid creating evidence that could be requested
why: Forensic readiness depends on agreed procedures and access to provider-side data. Late collection, informal promises and disabled logging weaken or destroy evidence.

q: A configuration management database lists server owners, but a post-incident review finds it was months out of date, slowing impact analysis. What is the BEST improvement?
opts: Restricting updates to a single review at the end of each year to save effort
Removing owner and status fields from every entry to simplify the records
Printing the database every month and filing the report with the auditors
Automated discovery that continuously updates configuration items
why: Cloud assets change constantly, so discovery must feed the record. Printing, annual updates and removing fields do not keep it accurate.

q: Which TWO controls MOST directly harden remote administrative access to cloud virtual machines? (Choose two.)
opts: Key- or certificate-based secure shell authentication with multi-factor authentication
Allowing remote desktop from any internet address
Leaving default accounts enabled
Routing access through a bastion host with session recording
Sharing one local administrator password among all engineers
why: Strong authentication and a controlled, recorded entry point reduce risk. Open remote desktop, shared passwords and default accounts raise it.

q: Which TWO statements about DNSSEC and VPNs are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A VPN removes the need for authentication on the target systems
DNSSEC signs DNS records so resolvers can verify authenticity and integrity
Both provide protection for data at rest
A VPN encrypts traffic across an untrusted network but extends the network to the endpoint
DNSSEC encrypts the content of DNS queries for privacy
why: DNSSEC gives authenticity and integrity, not confidentiality; VPNs protect data in transit but still require endpoint and identity controls. Neither protects data at rest.

q: Which THREE belong in operating system hardening for cloud virtual machines? (Choose three.)
opts: Leaving vendor default passwords for convenience
Monitoring for configuration drift
Running every service as an administrator
Applying an approved baseline such as a consensus benchmark
Removing unused services, accounts and ports
why: Baselines, drift monitoring and attack surface reduction are core hardening steps. Default passwords and excessive privilege weaken systems.

q: Which TWO activities are part of evidence management? (Choose two.)
opts: Sharing evidence through a public link for convenience
Editing files on the original evidence drive to annotate them
Storing items in secured, access-controlled locations with integrity hashes
Assigning unique identifiers and logging every transfer of the item
why: Tracking and secure storage preserve admissibility. Altering originals or sharing publicly destroys integrity.

q: A honeypot is a preventive control that blocks attacks before they reach production.
opts: True
False
why: Honeypots detect and study attackers using decoys; they do not block traffic and must be isolated.

q: Placing a host in maintenance mode lets its workloads migrate before servicing.
opts: True
False
why: This enables patching without downtime when the cluster has spare capacity.

q: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 contains 93 controls grouped into four themes.
opts: True
False
why: The themes are organizational, people, physical and technological.

q: DNSSEC provides confidentiality for DNS queries.
opts: True
False
why: DNSSEC provides authenticity and integrity of DNS data; query privacy needs encrypted DNS transport.

q: Incident management and problem management are the same process with different names.
opts: True
False
why: Incident management restores service; problem management removes underlying causes of recurring incidents.

q: COBIT 2019 is a governance and management framework for enterprise IT.
opts: True
False
why: COBIT 2019 from ISACA helps align IT with business goals and manage risk.

q: Cluster resilience such as storage replication removes the need for backups.
opts: True
False
why: Replication copies deletions and corruption too; backups protect against them.

q: A customer wants a repeatable weekly inventory of known weaknesses across hundreds of virtual machines, ranked by severity. Which activity is the BEST fit?
opts: An annual penetration test limited to the internet-facing web application of the business
A tabletop exercise on the ransomware response plan
A red team exercise that attempts to reach executives' mailboxes
An authenticated vulnerability scan with results tracked to remediation
why: Assessments are broad, repeatable and rank known weaknesses; penetration tests and red team exercises are narrower and prove exploitability, and tabletops rehearse response.

q: Before running a penetration test against workloads in a public cloud, the customer should confirm the provider's testing policy and obtain written authorization.
opts: True
False
why: Unauthorized testing can breach contract and law, and scope must avoid attacking the provider's shared infrastructure.

q: A SOC receives thousands of alerts with no context and cannot tell which matter. Which improvement would MOST help prioritization?
opts: Extending log retention from ninety days to seven years without changing alert content
Feeding curated threat intelligence into the SIEM and SOAR tools to enrich alerts with context
Turning off all low-severity detections so that analysts only see the most severe signals
Replacing analyst review with a single static firewall rule set for all environments
why: Threat intelligence adds context such as known indicators and adversary behavior, which helps rank alerts. Longer retention, disabled detections and static rules do not give context.

q: A machine-learning anomaly detector reports nothing for weeks, until it emerges that an administrator quietly disabled rules on a network security group and turned off flow logging. What was overlooked?
opts: Monitoring must also verify that controls and log sources are active and alert on changes
Anomaly detectors should be replaced by manual review of every packet that crosses the network boundary
Administrators should hold no privileges at all, which removes the need for monitoring
The detector should be trained on fewer features so that it generates fewer alerts
why: Intelligent monitoring includes watching the health of the controls and telemetry that feed it, so a silent change is itself an alert. Packet-level manual review and zero privileges are impractical, and fewer features do not fix blind spots.

q: All hosts in a cluster are healthy, but a guest virtual machine has stopped responding because of an operating system fault. Which measure addresses guest OS availability?
opts: Guest health monitoring with automatic restart and tested guest backups
Placing the host in maintenance mode so that the guest migrates to a different server in the cluster
Adding more physical storage to the cluster to increase raw capacity
Raising the hypervisor patch level on every host in the cluster
why: Host clustering protects against host failure, so a faulty guest needs its own health checks, restart logic and recoverable backups. Maintenance mode, extra storage and host patching do not fix a guest fault.

q: A cluster automatically moves virtual machines between hosts to balance load and keep response times steady. Which capability is this?
opts: Snapshot scheduling to preserve guest state at fixed times
Maintenance mode used to evacuate a host before servicing
Distributed resource scheduling or dynamic optimization
Storage replication to a secondary site for disaster recovery
why: Distributed resource scheduling places and rebalances workloads automatically. Maintenance mode is for planned servicing, replication provides recovery and snapshots preserve state.

q: After a major outage an organization wants a standing practice that turns incident reviews and audit findings into tracked, measured improvements. Which ITIL practice is this?
opts: Continual service improvement
Release management
Capacity management
Deployment management
why: Continual improvement measures service results and converts lessons into owned actions. Release and deployment management control how changes go live, and capacity management plans resource demand.

q: A European retailer uses a cloud provider whose support staff in another country may access personal data. Which mechanism BEST allows this transfer to be lawful if the country lacks an adequacy decision?
opts: The provider's marketing assurance of high security
Standard contractual clauses supported by a transfer impact assessment
A statement in the privacy policy that data may be transferred to other countries
Encrypting the data with a key the provider holds
why: SCCs with an assessment of destination laws are the standard contract-based safeguard. A policy statement alone is not a lawful mechanism, marketing is not a safeguard and provider-held encryption does not address legal access.

q: A company is the controller of customer data and uses a SaaS processor. A breach occurs at the processor. Which statement is MOST accurate about accountability?
opts: Accountability transfers entirely to the processor
No accountability exists for the controller because the processor suffered the breach
The controller remains accountable to regulators and individuals, and the processor must notify the controller
Only the individuals affected are accountable
why: Outsourcing processing does not outsource accountability. The processor has duties to notify and assist, but the controller answers to regulators.

q: An auditor asks for evidence that a SaaS provider's security controls operated effectively over the last year. Which report is MOST appropriate?
opts: SOC 2 Type I
SOC 2 Type II
A self-published marketing white paper
SOC 3 general-use summary
why: Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period. Type I examines design at a point in time, white papers are unverified and SOC 3 is a general summary without detailed testing.

q: A customer wants a comparable public view of a provider's assurance before choosing between two vendors. Which resource is MOST suitable?
opts: The CSA STAR registry entries for each provider
The providers' social media accounts
A competitor's sales brochure comparing the two providers
An internal list of preferred vendors
why: STAR is a public registry with self-assessments and third-party attestations aligned to the Cloud Controls Matrix. Social media and brochures are unaudited and internal preference lists do not provide evidence.

q: A US healthcare organization that is a HIPAA covered entity wants to host patient records with a cloud provider. Which contractual document is typically REQUIRED between the two?
opts: A non-compete agreement
A marketing co-branding agreement
A business associate agreement
A software escrow agreement only
why: Under HIPAA, a cloud provider that handles protected health information is a business associate and must sign such an agreement with the covered entity. The other documents do not satisfy the requirement.

q: A court order requires a company to produce emails stored in a cloud service. Which cloud-specific consideration is MOST important in the eDiscovery plan?
opts: Whether the provider's data centers hold a current ISO/IEC 27001 certificate
How many regions the provider operates around the world
The provider's published uptime percentage for its email service during the last year
Knowing where the data is held, how a legal hold is applied and what the provider will support
why: Location, hold mechanisms and provider support determine whether the company can preserve and produce data. Uptime, regional footprint and certification matter for availability and assurance but do not decide whether data can be preserved and produced.

q: Management decides to buy cyber insurance to cover part of the financial loss from a major breach. How is this risk treatment BEST classified?
opts: Risk acceptance, because no action is taken
Risk transfer, which does not remove accountability or the need for controls
