Risk mitigation, because the likelihood of a breach is reduced by the insurer
Risk avoidance, because the risk no longer exists
why: Insurance moves part of the financial impact to another party but leaves likelihood and legal accountability. Avoidance means stopping the activity, acceptance means retaining the risk and mitigation reduces likelihood or impact through controls.

q: A department starts using a free file-sharing service to exchange customer data without telling IT. Which response is MOST appropriate?
opts: Ignore it because the department owns the data
Discover the usage, assess the risk and offer an approved alternative
Encrypt the service's servers on the department's behalf
Terminate the employees immediately without any review of the business need
why: Shadow IT should be discovered, risk-assessed and replaced with a sanctioned option. Ignoring leaves compliance gaps, summary dismissal ignores process and customers cannot encrypt another company's servers.

q: A provider announces a new subprocessor in another jurisdiction. Which customer action is BEST?
opts: Review the subprocessor, exercise any right to object and reassess transfers
Cancel the contract without reading the terms
Remove the provider's logo from the website
Accept it automatically because the provider has a strong reputation and certifications
why: Contracts and GDPR give customers visibility and a say in subprocessors; review and reassess. Automatic acceptance and cancelling without review do not manage risk.

q: What is the main difference between due diligence and due care?
opts: Due care applies only to providers and due diligence only to customers
Due diligence is the response taken after an incident, while due care happens before any incident
They are legal terms with identical meanings
Due diligence is investigating before a decision; due care is acting responsibly to protect assets afterwards
why: Diligence is the research performed up front, such as vendor assessment; care is the ongoing practice of protection. They are related but not identical and apply to both parties.

q: A project plans to use customers' behavioral data to train a recommendation model at large scale. Which privacy activity is MOST appropriate before processing begins?
opts: Delete all existing consent records before starting the project
Publish the training dataset to the public
Conduct a data protection impact assessment
Wait for a data subject complaint
why: Large-scale profiling is the type of high-risk processing for which a DPIA is expected before it starts. The other options increase risk.

q: A US provider receives a legal demand from its government for data stored in a European region belonging to a European customer. Which mitigation BEST limits the provider's ability to hand over readable data?
opts: A longer password for the console
Customer-held keys so the provider cannot decrypt the data
A larger service level agreement credit if the provider discloses data
Moving the account to a cheaper pricing tier
why: If the provider lacks the key, it cannot produce readable content. SLA credits, pricing tiers and passwords do not affect legal access.

q: Which TWO items should be in a cloud service contract to protect the customer on exit? (Choose two.)
opts: A clause preventing the customer from ever changing provider
A provider right to keep copies for its own analytics
Data return in a usable format within a defined period
Silence on data ownership
Verified deletion of remaining copies including backups
why: Return and verified deletion support reversibility. Lock-in clauses, provider retention for its own use and ambiguity work against the customer.

q: Which TWO are reasons customers rely on third-party audit reports for cloud providers? (Choose two.)
opts: Reports are produced by the customer itself
Reports remove the customer's compliance duties
Direct customer audits of large multi-tenant providers are usually impractical
Independent reports give comparable evidence of control design and operation
Providers are legally forbidden from being audited
why: Scale and multi-tenancy make direct audits impractical, and independent reports give assurance. Providers can be audited, customers retain obligations and independence means the reports are not self-produced.

q: Which TWO risk treatments reduce the likelihood or impact of a risk through action rather than shifting or retaining it? (Choose two.)
opts: Moving the risk to the provider by contract alone
Stopping the risky activity altogether
Documenting acceptance by the business owner
Buying insurance
Implementing additional security controls
why: Mitigation reduces the risk and avoidance removes the activity. Insurance and contracts transfer and documented acceptance retains it.

q: Which TWO statements about GDPR are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: It applies only to companies headquartered in the EU
It forbids any transfer of personal data outside the EU
It can apply to a non-EU company processing personal data of people in the EU
It exempts companies that use cloud providers
A processor must handle personal data only on the controller's documented instructions
why: GDPR has extraterritorial reach and binds processors by controller instructions. It is not limited to EU headquarters, has no cloud exemption and permits transfers under lawful mechanisms.

q: A SOC 2 Type I report describes how controls operated effectively over a period of months.
opts: True
False
why: Type I covers design at a point in time; Type II covers operating effectiveness over a period.

q: Moving to the cloud transfers accountability for compliance from the customer to the provider.
opts: True
False
why: The customer remains accountable even where the provider performs some controls.

q: ISO/IEC 27018 provides guidance on protecting personal data in public clouds.
opts: True
False
why: It addresses providers acting as processors of personally identifiable information.

q: Under GDPR a controller must notify the supervisory authority of a reportable breach within 72 hours of becoming aware.
opts: True
False
why: This is the statutory deadline unless the breach is unlikely to result in risk to individuals.

q: A legal hold overrides normal retention schedules for relevant data.
opts: True
False
why: Deletion of potentially relevant data must be suspended until counsel releases the hold.

q: CSA STAR Level 1 is a third-party certification performed by an independent auditor.
opts: True
False
why: Level 1 is a self-assessment; third-party audit or certification is Level 2.

q: Risk acceptance should be decided and documented by the business owner of the affected asset.
opts: True
False
why: Security advises, but the owner with authority over the business impact accepts residual risk.

q: Pseudonymized personal data is outside the scope of GDPR.
opts: True
False
why: Because the data can be re-identified with additional information, it remains personal data.

q: Data residency and data sovereignty refer to exactly the same concept.
opts: True
False
why: Residency is where data is stored; sovereignty concerns which country's laws govern it.

q: A European retailer contracts with a US-headquartered cloud provider that stores the retailer's data in a Frankfurt region. Which US law can still be used to compel that provider to produce the data?
opts: The CLOUD Act
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act
FERPA
NERC CIP standards
why: The CLOUD Act lets US authorities compel a US provider to produce data in its possession, custody or control wherever it is stored, which is why customer-held keys and contract terms matter for European data. FERPA covers education records, Sarbanes-Oxley covers financial reporting controls and NERC CIP covers the bulk electric system.

q: A company needs a defensible method for forensic work after a cloud breach and wants standards covering collection of evidence, the suitability of the investigation method, analysis and the overall process. Which set of standards matches?
why: The 27037 to 27043 series covers evidence handling, method assurance, analysis and investigation processes. The other sets cover management systems, continuity and risk, or product evaluation and cloud vocabulary and supplier relationships.

q: A learning platform stores student grades and records for a US school district in a cloud service. Which law is MOST directly relevant to this data?
opts: NERC CIP
PCI DSS
FERPA
HIPAA
why: FERPA protects student education records. HIPAA covers health information, PCI DSS covers payment cards and NERC CIP covers the bulk electric system.

q: A Canadian retailer uses a cloud analytics provider in another country to process customer purchase histories. Which statement about its accountability is MOST accurate under PIPEDA?
opts: Accountability ends once the contract with the processor has been signed and filed
No accountability exists for private-sector data, because privacy law applies only to governments
The retailer remains accountable for personal information it transfers for processing, including abroad
Only the provider is accountable because it holds the data
why: PIPEDA keeps the organization accountable for information in the hands of processors and requires comparable protection. The other statements deny continuing accountability.

q: A company discovers a breach of electronic health records held by a business associate that stores them in the cloud. In which time frame must affected individuals generally be notified under US health privacy rules?
opts: Within 72 hours to the individuals directly, regardless of the facts of the breach
Within 24 hours of the first alert, whether or not a breach is confirmed
Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery
Only after the next annual audit
why: The breach notification rule requires notice without unreasonable delay and not later than 60 days after discovery. The 72-hour figure is the GDPR deadline for notifying the authority, not the individuals.

q: A team begins planning a new service that profiles customers' behavior across devices. Which activity BEST identifies privacy risks to individuals and the controls to address them before launch?
opts: A privacy impact assessment performed during design
A cost estimate performed by procurement during vendor selection
A penetration test performed shortly after launch by an external team
A disaster recovery drill performed after launch to rehearse the failover plan
why: A privacy impact assessment at design time finds risks to individuals and changes the design. The other activities test security, recovery or cost.

q: An auditor reviewing a SaaS provider's SOC report notes that it covers only the provider's main application and excludes the analytics module the customer actually uses. What should the customer do?
opts: Assume the whole provider is covered by the clean opinion, since the auditor signed it
Treat the analytics module as unassured, ask for scope extension or compensating evidence and apply customer controls
Ignore the exclusion, because audit reports do not list scope and apply to every service
Accept the report as it stands, because it was issued by a well-known audit firm
why: Scope statements define what is assured; excluded services need other evidence. A clean opinion on one service does not extend to another, and the firm's reputation does not change scope.

q: A company wants a report on a provider's controls that is relevant to financial reporting and is available under an international standard rather than a US one. Which pairing is MOST accurate?
opts: ISAE 3000 produces a SOC 1 report only
ISAE 3402 corresponds to SOC 1 under SSAE 18
SSAE 18 corresponds to ISO/IEC 27018 certification
ISAE 3402 corresponds to a PCI assessment
why: ISAE 3402 is the international standard for reports on controls relevant to financial reporting, equivalent in role to SOC 1 under SSAE 18. The other pairings mismatch standards.

q: A company's security leader wants control owners to evaluate their own risks and controls regularly, with independent validation afterwards, to keep ownership close to the business. Which technique is this?
opts: Risk and control self-assessment
A disaster recovery full interruption test
A black-box penetration test
A business impact analysis
why: Risk and control self-assessment lets control owners assess themselves and is then validated independently. Penetration testing, recovery tests and BIAs are different activities.

q: A utility moves a monitoring system for part of the bulk electric system to a cloud service. Which regulatory regime MUST the project consider?
opts: NERC CIP standards
FERPA
GAPP
SOX Section 404
why: NERC CIP sets mandatory cybersecurity requirements for bulk electric system entities. FERPA concerns education records, SOX concerns financial reporting and GAPP is a privacy framework.

q: Analysis shows a company cannot meet a country's data residency law for a planned cloud analytics feature, and management cancels the feature rather than launch it. Which risk treatment is this?
opts: Risk transfer
Risk avoidance
Risk sharing
Risk acceptance
why: Avoidance removes the risk by not starting, or by stopping, the activity that creates it. Sharing and transfer divide or move the consequence to another party, and acceptance knowingly keeps the risk.

q: A business rule says that a cloud provider's breach notice must reach the customer faster than the customer's own regulatory deadline. Which place BEST captures this requirement?
opts: The customer's internal wiki, which describes the provider's duties as the customer understands them
The provider's public marketing page describing how quickly incidents are handled
The contract's breach notification clause with a shorter notice period than the regulatory deadline
An informal email from the account manager promising prompt notice of any incident
why: Contract terms make notice periods enforceable. Marketing pages, informal emails and internal wikis do not bind the provider.

q: A software company depends on a small vendor for a critical component and fears the vendor may fail financially. Which contractual protection BEST addresses this risk?
opts: A warranty that the vendor will never go out of business, stated in the contract
A promise to review the vendor annually without access to its materials
A non-disclosure agreement alone, signed by the vendor and the customer's legal team
Escrow of source code or configuration with a neutral party, with release conditions
why: Escrow gives access to critical assets if the vendor fails. Warranties of permanence, reviews without access and NDAs do not secure continuity.

q: A company's cloud policy states which services may be bought, which data classes they may hold and who approves exceptions. What problem is this policy MOST directly designed to reduce?
opts: License fees for operating systems
Hardware failure in the provider's data center
Latency between two cloud regions
Unsanctioned shadow IT adoption
why: A cloud computing policy defines acceptable services, data classes and approvals, which limits shadow IT. The other problems are technical or financial.

q: Which TWO statements about audit scope statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A clean opinion covers all services the provider sells
A report assures only the services, locations and period named in its scope
Customer-side controls are often excluded and must be implemented by the customer
Excluded subservice organizations are automatically assured
Scope statements are written for marketing and can be ignored
why: Scope limits what is assured, and users must supply their own complementary controls. Other statements overstate coverage.

q: Which TWO items appear among the privacy frameworks and standards named for cloud privacy requirements? (Choose two.)
opts: ISO/IEC 27036 as a privacy law
Generally Accepted Privacy Principles with ten principles
NERC CIP as a data subject rights regulation
Common Criteria as a privacy framework
ISO/IEC 27018 for protecting personal data in public clouds
why: ISO/IEC 27018 and GAPP are privacy standards or frameworks. ISO/IEC 27036 concerns supplier relationships, NERC CIP is electric sector security and Common Criteria evaluates products.

q: Which THREE items belong in a cloud contract to support exit and accountability? (Choose three.)
opts: Right to audit or access to independent assurance reports
Data return and deletion terms with evidence of deletion
A ban on the customer ever terminating the contract
Breach notification timelines and subprocessor controls
A clause stating the provider owns customer data
why: Data return, notification, subprocessor and audit terms support exit and accountability. Provider data ownership and no termination undermine the customer.

q: HIPAA breach notification to individuals may take place up to 60 days after discovery of a breach, but must not be unreasonably delayed.
opts: True
False
why: The rule requires notice without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days.

q: A privacy impact assessment is performed before a system launches so privacy risks to individuals can change the design.
opts: True
False
why: It is a design-time review; the DPIA is the GDPR's formal version for high-risk processing.

q: A SOC report that excludes a subservice organization assures the controls of that subservice organization.
opts: True
False
why: Excluded subservice organizations are not assured by the report; customers need other evidence.

q: A master service agreement sets general terms while a statement of work defines specific deliverables.
opts: True
False
why: The SOW operates under the MSA; the SLA sets measurable service levels.

q: Risk transfer and risk sharing are interchangeable terms in the outline's list of treatments.
opts: True
False
why: The outline lists avoid, mitigate, transfer, share and accept as separate treatments.

q: PCI DSS version 4.0.1 is the current version of the standard.
opts: True
False
why: Version 4.0.1 is the current edition of the PCI Data Security Standard.

q: ISO/IEC 27050 is a standard for electronic discovery.
opts: True
False
why: It is a multi-part standard covering the eDiscovery process from identification to production.

q: A firm wants a general enterprise risk management standard of principles, framework and process that is not specific to IT. Which should it choose?
opts: ISO/IEC 27001, which certifies an information security management system
A SOC 2 report, which attests to a service provider's controls
PCI DSS, which sets requirements for protecting payment card data
why: ISO 31000 is the general risk management guideline. ISO/IEC 27001 is security-management specific, PCI DSS is a payment standard and a SOC 2 report is an attestation, not a framework to adopt.

q: Which indicator would be the MOST useful key risk indicator for the risk of cloud misconfiguration?
opts: The number of cloud provider marketing emails received by the security team
The trend in publicly exposed storage and critical findings open past their deadline
Annual revenue of the business units that use the cloud environment
The total number of employees who work in the cloud engineering department
why: A key risk indicator signals rising exposure early and links to the risk, such as exposed resources and overdue findings. Headcount, revenue and marketing volume say nothing about misconfiguration.

q: A company buys cyber risk insurance and concludes that its security controls can be reduced. Which statement is MOST accurate?
opts: Insurance transfers part of the financial loss, insurers expect baseline controls and accountability stays
Insurance removes the likelihood of an incident, which makes risk assessment unnecessary
Insurance eliminates regulatory fines in every jurisdiction regardless of how the incident arose
Insurance shifts legal accountability to the cloud provider, so customer controls become optional
why: Insurance is risk transfer of some financial impact, often conditional on controls and subject to exclusions. It does not remove accountability, likelihood or the need to assess risk.

q: A customer worries that a foreign authority could demand its data from the provider without the customer ever finding out. Which contract term helps MOST?
opts: A service level credit that is paid whenever the provider discloses customer data
A clause that lets the provider decide at its own discretion whether customers are informed
A commitment to notify the customer of government requests where the law allows and to challenge overbroad ones
A right to inspect the provider's data center after any disclosure has taken place
why: Notice and challenge commitments let the customer learn of a demand, object or seek protective orders, and keep control of the legal response. A credit compensates only after the fact, an inspection reveals nothing about the demand, and provider discretion removes the customer's visibility.

q: When two countries' laws conflict over the handling of data, a contract clause alone resolves the conflict because courts always honor the agreed terms.
opts: True
False
why: Mandatory law and regulators can override contract terms, so conflicts need legal analysis, location choices and technical controls.

q: An auditor must plan an engagement for a SaaS provider with no on-site access. What should the plan define FIRST?
opts: Scope, objectives and evidence sources such as provider reports, logs and API evidence
The final audit opinion, so that fieldwork can be limited to supporting it
Whether to skip the plan and perform only a walkthrough of the provider's website
A list of physical data centers to visit regardless of what the provider allows
why: Planning for a cloud audit depends on agreeing scope and objectives and identifying evidence that can actually be obtained remotely. Fixing the opinion first or insisting on site visits is neither possible nor independent.

q: A customer compares a provider's SOC 2 report with its own policy and finds five requirements unmet. What is the BEST next activity?
opts: Terminate the contract at once, since any gap makes the provider unusable
Ask the provider to rewrite the report so that it matches the customer's policy
Document the gaps and choose a treatment for each, such as compensating controls or contract changes
Ignore the gaps, because a SOC 2 report is a certification that the provider can never fail or lose
why: A gap analysis ends in documented treatment decisions. Reports cannot be rewritten, ignoring gaps is unsafe and automatic termination is disproportionate.

q: Which role is responsible for the day-to-day quality, definitions and metadata of a dataset, working under the data owner's policy?
opts: Regulator
Data subject
Data steward
Data processor
why: A data steward maintains quality and definitions for the owner. A processor handles data for a controller, the subject is the individual the data describes and a regulator supervises compliance.

q: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 refers to organizations that decide the purpose of processing as data fiduciaries and to individuals as data principals.
opts: True
False
why: These are the Act's equivalents of controller and data subject, with a Data Protection Board enforcing the law.
